text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PAGE: NewCorp (dedicated-eu-west-1) p99 latency SLO breach detected — p99 5.8s (>SLO 2s). Traffic spike concentrated on tenant:newcorp-123. Auto-escalation to on-call. Link: https://observability.redwood/internal/alerts/2245032100
Aisha (oncall SRE): I'm on it, picking up the page. Starting triage.
Priya (Support): Tom from NewCorp is on standby, looping him in. Tom?
Tom (AE - NewCorp): On the call. We're seeing timeouts for interactive search flows in EU users. Impacting about ~40% of requests. Please advise.
Miguel (SRE): Looking at metrics now — KCACHE hit-rate looks fine but tail token-latency spiking. Querying logs for tenant tag.
Devon (Infra Eng): Notified about warm pool capacity. Warm pool for eu-west-1 currently at 70% used. No infra alerts yet.
Aisha (oncall SRE): Initial investigation: this looks tenant-local (newcorp-123). Can we confirm whether requests are routing to dedicated pool nodes only or hitting mixed nodes?
Miguel (SRE): Log extract for newcorp-123 (last 10m):
```
2024-11-12T03:21:10Z [req] tenant=newcorp-123 model=redwood-7b quant=8bit seq=1024 latency=5900ms
2024-11-12T03:21:11Z [req] tenant=newcorp-123 model=redwood-7b quant=8bit seq=128 latency=5200ms
2024-11-12T03:21:12Z [req] tenant=newcorp-123 model=redwood-7b quant=8bit seq=768 latency=6100ms
```
Aisha (oncall SRE): Thanks. Pattern: high seq lengths + single-tenant traffic burst. Could be a change in their prompt distribution or a runaway job.
Priya (Support): Tom — can you confirm if NewCorp launched any batch jobs or a customer experiment around that time? Any internal deploys?
Tom (AE - NewCorp): I see a scheduled data-enrichment job started ~03:15 UTC which fanouts long-context prompts. Ops didn't expect it to be that heavy, pushing more LLM tokens than usual.
Aisha (oncall SRE): OK that pins it. Mitigation options: 1) Apply per-tenant rate throttle on newcorp-123 to protect shared pool, 2) Migrate their traffic to a reserved warm-failover pool in a different region (eu-central) if configured, 3) Isolate into dedicated shard (if available) — that takes time.
Devon (Infra Eng): We can flip a routing policy to DR region if NewCorp has failover enabled. Will take ~2-3m to update policy and for in-flight requests to drain.
Miguel (SRE): In parallel I'll push a soft throttle at the proxy layer limiting parallel streams to 20 for tenant=newcorp-123. That should bring p99 down while preserving best-effort service.
Aisha (oncall SRE): Miguel — execute the throttle. Use: `kubectl -n ingress patch configmap tenant-quotas --patch '{"data":{"newcorp-123":"streams=20"}}'`. After patch, I'll monitor p99 and KV cache pressure.
Miguel (SRE): Patch applied. Command output:
```
configmap/tenant-quotas patched
```
Miguel (SRE): Observability: p99 dropped from 5.8s -> 2.9s in 70s. p95 at 1.1s. KV cache miss rate unchanged. Looks like collapsing parallelism helped.
Aisha (oncall SRE): Good. Customer impact still present but reduced. Tom — want us to fully block the enrichment job or prefer a softer throttle?
Tom (AE - NewCorp): We need the job to finish, but please keep it slow. A 50% throttle is fine. We'll backoff the job on our side as well.
Priya (Support): Noted; telling customer ops we applied a soft quota to slow throughput. PR to update their on-call doc and inform downstream teams.
Devon (Infra Eng): I'm preparing DR route in case throttle isn't enough. Confirm: NewCorp has failover pool in eu-central with reserved warm nodes?
Tom (AE - NewCorp): Yes, we purchased a warm failover in eu-central. Enable if needed.
Aisha (oncall SRE): Plan: 1) Keep soft throttle (Miguel), 2) If p99 > 3.5s for next 3 min -> trigger migration to eu-central failover (Devon), 3) If still failing -> isolate tenant into its own dedicated shard (requires infra change, schedule 30–45m).
runbook-bot: Referenced runbook: VPC/Dedicated tenant SLO breach playbook — https://redwood.internal/runbooks/vpc-slo-breach. Follow section 2 (soft-throttle -> failover -> isolate).
Miguel (SRE): p99 currently 2.5s and trending down. I'll keep the limit for 15 minutes and then step down to 40 streams after confirming stabilization.
Aisha (oncall SRE): I'll update incident state to "Mitigated (soft throttle)" and handoff to next oncall in 30m if stable. Recording incident notes.
Priya (Support): Communicating to NewCorp engineering: "We've applied a temporary quota to slow the job; your ops team should coordinate to reschedule. Reach out on this thread for updates."
Tom (AE - NewCorp): Thanks, much appreciated. We'll throttle on our end and cancel any retries.
Devon (Infra Eng): FYI I primed the failover routing change; ready to flip in 90s if Miguel reports re-escalation.
Miguel (SRE): Dropping streams from 20 -> 40 (gentle increase) at 2245032360 to let job progress. p99 stable ~2.1s.
Aisha (oncall SRE): Good. Marking impact: "NewCorp interactive flows degraded from 03:15–03:40 UTC; mitigation via tenant soft-quota. No SLO breach after throttle. Recommend customer reschedule heavy batch and consider longer-term quota/ingress limits."
Priya (Support): Creating post-incident ticket with root cause: unplanned high-token batch job combined with long-sequence prompts. Action items: 1) Customer-side: enforce job rate limits; 2) Platform: consider auto-tenant-protection thresholds for large seq lengths; 3) Sales/AE: review failover purchase UX.
Tom (AE - NewCorp): We'll follow up internally and file a change to prevent recurrence. Appreciate the quick response.
Aisha (oncall SRE): Handoff: @Miguel will own stabilization for next 30m, @Devon on standby for failover, @Priya to handle comms. If anything regresses ping oncall. Closing the active page for now. :white_check_mark:
incident-bot: Incident state changed -> MITIGATED by Aisha. Pages cleared.
Miguel (SRE): Leaving a final log snippet for postmortem:
```
action=soft_throttle tenant=newcorp-123 old_limit=unlimited new_limit=20 applied_by=miguel duration=22m p99_before=5.8s p99_after=2.1s
```
Aisha (oncall SRE): Thanks team. I'll open a postmortem draft and link it to the runbook. Handoff complete. :thumbsup:
